Studio / Styles / The Great Wave off Kanagawa

The Great Wave off Kanagawa

Katsushika Hokusai, c. 1831

Colour woodblock print

Japanese woodblock print of a towering wave in Prussian blue and white.

Use this style

Katsushika Hokusai, The Great Wave off Kanagawa, c. 1831. Modern recut impression, c. 1930. Source on Wikimedia Commons. Licence: Public domain.

About the painting

The Great Wave is the best known print from Hokusai's series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, published around 1831 by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo. A wave about to break over three boats frames a small Mount Fuji in the distance. Hokusai was in his early seventies when he designed it.

Each colour was printed from its own carved woodblock, so the image is built from flat areas and crisp outlines. The deep blue is Prussian blue, a synthetic pigment then newly available in Japan, which was part of the series' appeal. The file used here is a faithful recut impression made around 1930 from the original design.

How it looks on your photo

The model brings the blue-and-cream palette and the claw-like curls of foam, and gives photos a flatter, printed look. It suits sea, sky and mountains. Fine detail such as fur and foliage turns into small, curling marks.
